hypothesis.statement: In cubic Li3OX antiperovskites (Pm-3m; O2- at the octahedron centre, X- at the cube corner, Li at the octahedron vertices), the Li vacancy hop barrier is set by the bottleneck between adjacent Li sites along the Li6O octahedron edge, which widens as the corner halide gets larger and the lattice expands. With stoichiometry, framework and hop mechanism fixed, replacing Cl- with Br- and then I- lowers the Li migration barrier monotonically, at the cost of a less stable cubic phase because the larger corner anion strains the octahedral framework.
hypothesis.rationale: Li3OX contains no reducible cation: Li+ is the only cation and O2- and X- are already fully reduced, so chemically Li metal has nothing to reduce, unlike thiophosphates (P5+) or Ge/Ti-bearing conductors. This is chemical reasoning, not a measurement. energy_above_hull measures thermodynamic stability of the phase itself, not survival against Li metal; it is a proxy and is treated as one. The quantity the goal actually asks about (reaction energy with Li metal, or reduction potential) is not measured, and no result this round can establish Li-metal stability directly. Fixing the framework and changing only the corner anion isolates lattice size/bottleneck width. If Br is no better than Cl, lattice expansion does not govern the barrier here, and later rounds should look at defect chemistry or mixed-anion ordering. If Br is better but I is not, there is an optimum, likely from cubic framework distortion or softening at large tolerance factor, arguing for Br-rich mixed compositions. Not tested this round: vacancy concentration needed for conduction (depends on aliovalent doping or LiX deficiency) and mixed Cl/Br compositions. A later round needs a doped arm, e.g. a divalent cation on Li paired with Li vacancies in the best parent, to show whether a low single-hop barrier survives realistic carrier generation. Model scope (a few hundred atoms, picoseconds) excludes grain-boundary transport, which matters in these materials; nothing here speaks to it. No measurements are on record yet.
hypothesis.prediction: Migration barrier orders Li3OCl > Li3OBr > Li3OI, with each step at least 0.03 eV. Energy above hull orders the opposite way: Li3OCl < Li3OBr < Li3OI. No absolute values are predicted because no measurements exist yet. The 0.03 eV step is a minimum effect size committed in advance so model noise cannot count as support; the model's barrier uncertainty is unknown, and if reported confidences show uncertainty larger than 0.03 eV the step size must be re-read against them.
hypothesis.falsification_criterion: The barrier claim is refuted if E_a(Li3OBr) >= E_a(Li3OCl) - 0.03 eV, or E_a(Li3OI) >= E_a(Li3OBr) - 0.03 eV. If Li3OI comes back flagged OOD or low-confidence, it cannot carry the verdict and the decision rests on the Cl -> Br comparison alone. Secondary: if the e_hull ordering Li3OCl < Li3OBr < Li3OI fails, the 'barrier bought at the cost of stability' half of the claim is wrong even if the barrier half survives.

batch_plan.strategy: Build three candidates in the same cubic Pm-3m antiperovskite framework, all at Li3OX stoichiometry with no dopants or vacancies beyond those the barrier calculation itself introduces. (1) Li3OCl: retrieve cubic Pm-3m Li3OCl as parent (O at body centre, Cl at corners, Li at face centres). (2) Li3OBr: from the Li3OCl parent substitute 100% Cl -> Br, keep space group and site assignments, relax lattice parameter and ionic positions. (3) Li3OI: from the same parent substitute 100% Cl -> I, same constraints and relaxation. Hold fixed across all three: the cubic framework, cation and anion site occupancies, supercell size for the barrier calculation, and the migration mechanism (single Li vacancy hopping between nearest-neighbour Li sites along the Li6O octahedron edge). Do not include partial Cl/Br or Br/I mixtures, doped variants, or other frameworks; they sit on neither side of the comparison. Measure migration_barrier and energy_above_hull for all three and report confidence and any proxy/OOD flags for each, so Li3OI can be excluded from the verdict if flagged OOD.

vetoes.reason: Li5IO6 is a periodate with IO6 octahedra and I in +7, not a Pm-3m Li3OX antiperovskite with a corner halide and Li6O framework, so it has no slot in the Cl -> Br -> I comparison that decides h1.

LiIO3 is an iodate with IO3 pyramids and I in +5, not a cubic Li3OX antiperovskite, so it cannot inform the controlled halide substitution in h1.

body.commentary:
No candidates approved, so the batch is empty this round. I checked structure type against h1 (Pm-3m Li3OX, X at the cube corner, O at the Li6O octahedron centre). In all three candidates the halogen is an oxyanion centre, acting as a cation, not a corner halide. Chemistry is charge-balanced and plausible: Li+, O2-, and the halogen in +7, +7 and +5. LiClO4 and LiIO3 are well-known salts, so implausible and unsynthesizable do not apply. There are no duplicates and nothing has been measured yet.

Independent of h1, all three conflict with the Li-metal stability goal. Halogens in +5 and +7 are strong oxidizers that Li metal would be expected to reduce. No reaction energy is on record. This reinforces the veto but is not a separate category.

Notes for the Analyst:

(1) Retrieval appears to have matched on element set rather than structure type. It needs to return the Pm-3m Li3OCl, Li3OBr and Li3OI entries. No database IDs or existence claims are quoted because none are in the notebook. A Br entry is required, and none is in this batch. If an ordered Pm-3m Li3OI cannot be found, h1's fallback applies and the verdict rests on Cl -> Br alone.

(2) energy_above_hull is a proxy. It measures stability against competing phases in Li-X-O space, not reactivity toward Li. A low e_hull is at best a necessary condition. Read the e_hull ordering as a test of h1's secondary cubic-phase-stability claim, not as a Li-compatibility ranking. A direct Li-stability statement needs a reaction or decomposition energy against Li metal, which is absent.

(3) Computed barriers describe an idealised single vacancy hop in a perfect cell of at most a few hundred atoms. They say nothing about grain-boundary transport, hydrated or Li-deficient phases, or bulk conductivity. If barriers come from short MD rather than a path calculation, picosecond sampling may not resolve hops. Treat those values as poorly constrained, and check whether their uncertainty exceeds the 0.03 eV step committed in h1.

(4) Li3OI is the likeliest to be flagged OOD or low-confidence. If it is, it cannot carry the verdict. For Li3OBr, and especially Li3OI, check that the relaxed cell stays Pm-3m. Symmetry lowering would break the fixed-framework premise, and the comparison would then not test h1 as stated.

hypothesis.statement: In cubic Pm-3m Li3OX antiperovskites (O2- at the centre of the Li6O octahedron, X- at the cube corner), the Li vacancy hop runs along the edge of the Li6O octahedron and its barrier is set by the width of that bottleneck, which widens as the lattice expands. Fully replacing the corner Cl- with Br- expands the lattice and lowers the Li vacancy migration barrier; replacing Br- with I- lowers it further. The same expansion destabilises the cubic phase against competing Li-X-O phases. This is h1 run again with tighter reading rules, not a new claim: h1 was never tested because round 1 retrieved only off-spec halogen oxyanion salts and zero measurements exist.
hypothesis.rationale: This is the cheapest claim on the table that can die: two candidates (Li3OCl, Li3OBr) decide it and the third (Li3OI) extends it. The Cl -> Br step is the single comparison most wanted settled. It could plausibly fail: the vacancy hop is between Li sites on an octahedron centred on O2-, so the Li-O distance may not follow the halide-driven expansion closely, and the more polarisable corner anion could reshape the saddle point in a way geometry alone does not predict. If Br does not beat Cl by 0.03 eV, the 'bottleneck width set by the corner halide' picture is wrong for this framework, and the next lever would be the Li6O octahedron itself (e.g. aliovalent doping on the Li site at fixed halide). Moving to a different hypothesis would treat a retrieval failure as a scientific result; the fix is the batch construction. What this round cannot answer: per the established heuristic, energy_above_hull is used only for cubic-phase stability against Li-X-O competitors and says nothing about stability against Li metal; the goal's Li-stability axis stays untested until a reaction or decomposition energy against Li metal is added as a scored property. That measurement is missing. What would change my mind: a Pm-3m Li3OBr barrier within 0.03 eV of, or above, Li3OCl at uncertainty <= 0.03 eV. If Li3OCl and Li3OBr pass and Li3OI fails the symmetry or OOD check, a later round needs a different third arm that expands the lattice without symmetry loss, e.g. isotropic strain on Li3OCl at fixed composition, to separate lattice expansion from halide identity.
hypothesis.prediction: With all three cells still Pm-3m after relaxation and each barrier from a path (NEB-type) calculation on the single-vacancy hop along the octahedron edge: E_a(Li3OBr) <= E_a(Li3OCl) - 0.03 eV, and E_a(Li3OI) <= E_a(Li3OBr) - 0.03 eV. energy_above_hull (eV/atom) orders as Li3OCl < Li3OBr < Li3OI. No absolute values are given; the notebook holds none.
hypothesis.falsification_criterion: Primary (two arms): the barrier claim is refuted if E_a(Li3OBr) >= E_a(Li3OCl) - 0.03 eV, with both cells confirmed Pm-3m after relaxation and both reported barrier uncertainties <= 0.03 eV. Extension: if Cl -> Br survives, monotonic decrease is refuted if E_a(Li3OI) >= E_a(Li3OBr) - 0.03 eV, only if Li3OI is Pm-3m after relaxation, not OOD and not low-confidence; otherwise Li3OI is dropped and the verdict rests on Cl -> Br alone. Secondary: the stability-cost claim is refuted if the e_hull ordering Cl < Br < I fails among cells passing the symmetry check, even if the barrier half survives. Inconclusive (not refuted) if either decisive cell relaxes out of Pm-3m, a reported barrier uncertainty exceeds 0.03 eV, or a barrier comes from picosecond MD rather than a path calculation.

batch_plan.strategy: Exactly 3 candidates, all Pm-3m Li3OX antiperovskite prototype; stoichiometry, framework and hop path held fixed; only the corner-site halide changes, fully, in each arm. (1) Li3OCl: retrieve by prototype and space group (Pm-3m anti-perovskite, Li at octahedron vertices, O at octahedron centre, Cl at cube corner), not by element set. Reject any hit containing ClO4-, ClO3- or any halogen in a positive oxidation state. If no Pm-3m Li3OCl entry exists, stop and report it; do not substitute another structure. (2) Li3OBr: retrieve the Pm-3m entry by prototype; if none exists, build from the step-1 Li3OCl cell by 100% Cl -> Br on the corner site, then relax lattice parameter and positions. (3) Li3OI: 100% Cl -> I on the corner site of the step-1 cell, then relax; expect an OOD flag and pass it through unchanged. Do not include partial or mixed-halide cells (e.g. Li3OCl0.5Br0.5), any oxyanion salt (perchlorate, iodate, periodate), or any non-Pm-3m polymorph. The batch does not count as a test round unless Li3OCl and Li3OBr are both present before measurement is scheduled. For each cell record: migration_barrier (eV) from a path calculation for the single Li vacancy hop along the Li6O octahedron edge, with confidence and OOD flag; energy_above_hull (eV/atom) with confidence and proxy/OOD flags; space group after relaxation. Drop any cell no longer Pm-3m from the comparison rather than averaging it in.

proposal.summary: No hypothesis was refuted, because nothing was tested. The notebook holds 0 measurements, 0 candidates on the Pareto frontier, and 0 candidates with any measurement. h1 and h2 both closed INCONCLUSIVE. Both claimed that in cubic Pm-3m Li3OX antiperovskites, replacing Cl- with Br- and then I- lowers the Li vacancy migration barrier at the cost of cubic-phase stability. That claim is neither supported nor weakened. Both rounds failed at retrieval, not measurement. The only reliable negative result is procedural. Querying by the Li-O-halogen element set returned three halogen oxyanion salts: c-mp-1211142 Li5IO6 (I(+7)), c-mp-30301 LiClO4 (Cl(+7)) and c-mp-23384 LiIO3 (I(+5)). The Skeptic vetoed all three as off_spec. None is an antiperovskite, none has a reduced halide, and their high-valent halogens make them poor choices against Li metal on chemical grounds. This retrieval strategy is refuted as a way to reach the target structures and should not be run again. Not established: any Li migration barrier for any compound; any energy_above_hull for any compound; any reaction or decomposition energy against Li metal (required by an established standing order but never added to the objectives); and whether the pipeline can report a path-based barrier with a numerical uncertainty and a post-relaxation space group. No candidate can be recommended, because no measured candidate exists. Recommending Li3OCl or Li3OBr on literature reputation would break the evidence rule. This proposal describes the experiment that would produce the missing data: computational first, then laboratory.
synthesis_route: Computational (run first; it decides whether the lab work tests anything). Build cubic Pm-3m Li3OCl and Li3OBr by prototype substitution, not element-set retrieval: O at the octahedron centre (1a), halide at the cube corner (1b), Li at the octahedron vertices (3c). Build Li3OI the same way, as an extension only. Relax each cell, record the post-relaxation space group, and drop any cell that leaves Pm-3m.

Computational: for each cell that stays Pm-3m, compute three quantities. (a) A single Li-vacancy hop barrier along the Li6O octahedron edge by NEB, not picosecond MD, reported with uncertainty, confidence and OOD flag. (b) energy_above_hull in eV/atom. (c) Reaction energy against Li metal for Li3OX + n Li -> most stable product set, in eV/atom. If the pipeline cannot report a barrier uncertainty, record that and rewrite the falsification criteria before any lab step.

Conditions for steps 3-6 are starting points taken from published Li3OCl preparations. This campaign has not validated them, and each run must record its actual conditions. Dry the precursors: LiCl or LiBr at >=99.9%, and anhydrous LiOH. Dry each separately under dynamic vacuum (<10^-2 mbar) at 200 °C for 12 h, then transfer to an Ar glovebox with H2O and O2 each <1 ppm.

Primary hydroxide route: weigh 2 LiOH : 1 LiX by mole and grind in an agate mortar for 15 min. Load into a Ni crucible inside a quartz tube on a Schlenk line. Heat under continuous dynamic vacuum to 330-360 °C at 2 °C/min and hold for 24 h, so the vacuum removes the H2O from 2 LiOH + LiX -> Li3OX + H2O. Cool under vacuum and transfer to the glovebox without air exposure.

Cross-check hydroxide-free route: mix Li2O and LiX 1:1 by mole and ball-mill in a ZrO2 jar sealed under Ar. Press a pellet, seal it in an evacuated quartz ampoule inside a Ni liner, and anneal. The purpose is to separate true Li3OX from the hydroxide phase Li2OHX, which is easily confused with it and can leave residual H.
Transport pellets: cold-press at 300-400 MPa in a die inside the glovebox. Sputter Au, or press Li foil, onto both faces depending on the measurement. Record relative density geometrically.
validation_protocol: Computational (synthesis steps 1-2): NEB barrier pair, energy_above_hull and reaction energy against Li. The Li3OCl/Li3OBr barrier pair alone decides the primary arm of h2.

Powder XRD with Rietveld refinement (Cu Kα, airtight Kapton or dome holder): shows whether each product is single-phase cubic Pm-3m and gives its lattice parameter. It also tests whether Br expands the lattice relative to Cl, which is the premise of the bottleneck mechanism.
FTIR (O-H stretch region) and 1H MAS NMR: show whether the sample contains OH. A sample with OH is Li2OHX or a mixture, and its transport data cannot enter the comparison.

Variable-temperature EIS on Au | Li3OX | Au pellets, 25-150 °C in 10 °C steps, 1 MHz-1 Hz, under Ar. Fit bulk and grain-boundary arcs separately. Gives the Arrhenius activation energy of the bulk arc, with fit uncertainty, for Cl and Br.
7Li NMR spin-lattice relaxation versus temperature: gives a local hop activation energy less contaminated by grain boundaries than EIS. This is the lab quantity closest to the single-hop NEB barrier.
DC polarization on Au-blocked pellets: gives electronic conductivity. Electronic leakage would let a Li metal interface keep growing even if the interface is thermodynamically benign.
Li | Li3OX | Li symmetric cells: EIS every 10 h at open circuit for 100 h, then galvanostatic cycling. Shows whether interfacial resistance grows with time in contact with Li.
XPS of the Li-contacted surface after the symmetric-cell test, with Ar-sputter depth profiling: shows whether new reduced species form at the Li interface, testing the computed reaction energy.
falsification_criteria: All numbers below are decision thresholds set by the campaign, not predicted values. Computational, primary arm: the halide-expansion barrier claim is refuted if E_a(Li3OBr) >= E_a(Li3OCl) - 0.03 eV, provided both cells are Pm-3m after relaxation, both barriers are NEB path-based, and both reported uncertainties are <= 0.03 eV. The result is inconclusive, not refuted, if either cell leaves Pm-3m, either uncertainty exceeds 0.03 eV, or either barrier comes from MD.

Computational extension (Br -> I), evaluated only if Cl -> Br survives: monotonic decrease is refuted if E_a(Li3OI) >= E_a(Li3OBr) - 0.03 eV. Li3OI counts only if it stays Pm-3m and is neither OOD nor low-confidence; otherwise it is dropped.
Computational stability cost: the 'barrier bought at the cost of phase stability' claim is refuted if the energy_above_hull ordering Cl < Br < I fails among cells that pass the symmetry check.

Computational Li-metal stability: the 'stable against Li metal' requirement is refuted for a composition if its computed reaction energy with Li is negative by more than its reported uncertainty. energy_above_hull can neither rescue nor refute this criterion.

Lab phase: a composition is excluded from all transport comparisons if PXRD shows reflections not indexable to Pm-3m above about 3 wt% in Rietveld, or if FTIR or 1H NMR detects OH. If Li3OBr cannot be made phase-pure by either route, the lab test of the Br arm is inconclusive, not passed.

Lab transport: the barrier claim is refuted if the activation energy for Li3OBr is >= the activation energy for Li3OCl - 0.03 eV, with both fit uncertainties <= 0.03 eV. This applies to the bulk-arc EIS activation energy and, separately, to the 7Li NMR activation energy. If EIS and NMR disagree in direction, the result is inconclusive and is reported as such.

Lab Li contact: the Li-stability claim is refuted for a composition if any of the following holds: interfacial resistance in Li | Li3OX | Li at open circuit more than doubles over 100 h; XPS shows new reduced species beyond what the composition already contains; or electronic conductivity from DC polarization exceeds 10^-4 of the bulk ionic conductivity measured on the same pellet.
caveats: Capability boundary: the atomistic models reach a few hundred atoms over picoseconds. They say nothing about bulk mechanical properties; long-timescale kinetics, interphase growth or degradation at a Li anode; grain-boundary and microstructural effects, which usually dominate pressed-pellet EIS; or device-level performance, dendrite suppression, cost or manufacturability. Every lab measurement from EIS onward probes something the models cannot, so agreement or disagreement there is new information, not a check on a model prediction.

Proxy: energy_above_hull was the only declared stability objective. It ranks phase stability against competing Li-X-O phases and is not stability against Li metal. The established order to replace it with a reaction energy against Li was never carried out.

Proxy: the single-vacancy NEB barrier stands in for transport. It omits vacancy formation energy and defect concentration, so it is not the same quantity as a conductivity activation energy, and the two can legitimately differ.
Proxy: the 'low-electronegativity or reduction-tolerant anion' heuristic in the seed strategy is chemical intuition, not a measurement.
OOD: none recorded, because nothing was computed. Li3OI is the composition most likely to be flagged, and the criteria already drop it in that case.

Unseparated: it is unknown whether the pipeline reports per-barrier uncertainty and relaxed symmetry. If it does not, the primary criterion can only return INCONCLUSIVE and must be rewritten before any compute is spent.
Unseparated: Li3OX and Li2OHX are hard to tell apart by XRD alone, so the FTIR/NMR check is mandatory. EIS cannot fully separate bulk from grain-boundary transport in poorly densified pellets.

Process: two rounds were spent on a retrieval strategy that could not return the target structures. Under the standing orders, no further Li3OX hypothesis counts as a test until both Pm-3m cells exist and the Skeptic has passed them.
Synthesis temperatures and times are starting conditions taken from published Li3OCl preparations and were not validated by this campaign.
